chunks: 1- Musa ibn al-Qasim from Safwan and Ibn Abi Umayr from Umar ibn Udhaynah from Burayd ibn Muawiya al-Ajli said:

I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about a man who performed Hajj while he did not know this matter (Imamate), then God granted him knowledge and devotion to it. Is the Hajj of Islam obligatory upon him, or has he fulfilled his duty? He said: He has fulfilled his duty, and if he performed again, it would be more beloved to me. I asked him about a man who performed while he was from one of the categories of the People of the Qibla, a Nasib (devout but not of the Ahl al-Bayt), then God granted him and he knew this matter. Does he fulfill the Hajj of Islam? He said: He fulfills it, it is more beloved to me. And he said: Every deed he performed while in the state of his Nasib and misguidance, then God granted him and he was made to know the Wilayah, he is rewarded for it except for Zakat, for he returns it, because he placed it in its non-places, because it is for the People of the Wilayah. As for the Prayer, Hajj, and Fasting, there is no need for him to make them up.

2- As for what Muhammad ibn Ya'qub narrated from a number of our companions from Sahl ibn Ziyad from Ali ibn Mahziyar who said: Ibrahim ibn Muhammad ibn Imran al-Hamadani wrote to Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) saying: I performed Hajj while I was opposing (the Wilayah), and I was single, so I entered performing Tamattu' with Umrah to Hajj. He wrote to him: Repeat your Hajj.

3- And what he also narrated from Muhammad ibn Ya'qub from a number of our companions from Ahmad ibn Muhammad and Sahl ibn Ziyad together from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Nasr from Ali ibn Abi Hamzah from Abu Basir from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: The Nasibi, when he knows (the Wilayah), upon him is the Hajj. And if he had already performed, the ruling in these two narrations is a type of preference (Istihbab) rather than obligation (Fard/Ijbab). And Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) explicitly stated this in the narration of Burayd al-Ajli in his saying: 'He has fulfilled his duty, and if he performed, it would be more beloved to me.' And this also indicates it.

4- What Muhammad ibn Ya'qub narrated from Ali ibn Ibrahim from his father from Ibn Abi Umayr from Umar ibn Udhaynah who said: I wrote to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) asking him about a man who performed while he did not know and was unaware of this matter, then God granted him knowledge and devotion to it. Is the Hajj of Islam upon him, or has he fulfilled God's duty? He said: He has fulfilled God's duty, and the Hajj is more beloved to me. And about a man who is from one of these categories of the People of the Qibla, a Nasib devout, then God granted him and he knew this matter. Is the Hajj of Islam fulfilled for him, or is it upon him to perform next year? He said: He performs, it is more beloved to me.

key_terms.التَّمَتُّعُ: A type of Hajj combining Umrah and Hajj
key_terms.نَاصِبٌ: One who opposes the Ahl al-Bayt (often used for early Sunnis)

ai.seo_question: Does a person need to repeat their Hajj if they were unaware of the Imamate of the Ahl al-Bayt at the time?
ai.summary: Shaykh al-Tusi synthesizes multiple narrations to establish that Hajj performed by the Nasib (opponent of the Ahl al-Bayt) or the ignorant is valid but not obligatory upon their conversion, distinguishing this from Zakat which must be repeated as it was given to non-Ahl al-Bayt. This ruling highlights the Shia theological emphasis on Wilayah as the criterion for the acceptance and perfection of acts of worship, while maintaining the continuity of basic Islamic pillars. The text clarifies that while the initial Hajj suffices for the Fard, performing it again is preferred (Istihbab) to demonstrate renewed devotion to the Imamate.
